Search highlights only (not a full fetch).

Remarks by Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, at the end of his visit to New York:

"Another objective we pursued, which is a very important one, was to convey to the world the country's positions regarding the war, and particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz."

"There are conditions set by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, and these conditions must be fulfilled for the Strait of Hormuz to be opened. Our mission was to convey these conditions both to the American side and to all other countries and the international community, so that they would be aware that Iran has a plan in this regard. Iran's conditions are entirely fair and logical, and if the Americans claim that they are seeking an agreement or a peaceful solution, we present this solution to them."

"Our plan, which became known as the seven-point plan, was conveyed to the Americans through the Qatari intermediary. Despite the remarks made by the US president, I said that we were awaiting an official response from the United States through the intermediaries. Today, one of the Qatari intermediaries held another meeting with us. We discussed various issues and exchanged ideas on how to facilitate the fulfillment of Iran's conditions and how these conditions could be met. They had some ideas, and we discussed them. They are going to raise this matter with the American side once again, and then the American side's final response will be conveyed to us through the Qatari intermediary. They hope this will be done by tomorrow."

"I will fly to Tehran in a few hours, and whenever the Qataris have a response, they know themselves how they can convey it to us. These communications and messages exchanged between the Qatari and Pakistani mediators had already existed. Now, in light of the plan presented by Iran, they have taken on a more serious form. If there is a response, the Qataris will convey it, and a decision will then be made in Tehran based on that response."

"We have seen that, over the past few hours, a media campaign has emerged in various outlets, with claims being made and statements attributed to Iran. I categorically state that there has been no change whatsoever in Iran's positions. Our conditions for reopening the Strait are clear. Our position on other issues is also clear. At present, there has been absolutely no discussion of any flexibility on our part."

"Our position is clear. At present, the only issue is the Strait of Hormuz. The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is also contingent upon the fulfillment of a number of conditions that we have communicated to the other side. I would ask that no attention be paid to the speculation or deliberate media narratives being created by certain outlets."
